dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) based on Linux file paths (/oscobol/src/), RECORDING MODE IS V with variable-length records, and FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE usage. Author 'UCA' and French comments suggest academic/educational context.
evidence: RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 100 to 30000
French display text: 'TRAITEMENT BACH STATISTIQUES VISITES'

purpose.domain_detail: Student exercise simulating batch processing of visit statistics and transaction records, likely for a university COBOL course (author 'UCA').
purpose.summary: A batch program that reads a visit file sequentially, displays each record, then writes a hardcoded transaction record to a transactions output file. It uses FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE to timestamp the transaction. French display messages suggest a francophone academic environment.

notable_features: RECORDING MODE IS V with variable-length records (up to 30000 bytes)
Duplicate data-name definitions (WS-CURRENT-DATE, WS-CURRENT-YEAR, etc.) across multiple 01-level records
Unix/Linux file paths in SELECT ASSIGN
PIC Z(1) used for END-OF-FILE flag (unusual)
PERFORM THRU pattern for paragraph range
verdict.notes: DATE-WRITTEN value '20201502' appears to be an invalid date (day 02, month 15). Duplicate data-names (WS-CURRENT-DATE, WS-CURRENT-YEAR, etc.) defined at multiple levels would cause compilation errors in strict compilers. The program has structural issues consistent with student work. One line slightly exceeds 72 characters (max_line_length=73).
